Depending on the version of linux you’re using, your package manager may be: apt for debian, pacman and yay for arch (i dont remember the rest they kinda suck frfr).

Where Windows stores files in paths such as C:/Users/${youruser}/PathToFIle and C:/Path/To/File, Linux(and other Unix-based OSes, including but not limited to MacOS).

There are multiple types of shells for Unix-based Operating Systems. The most common and default shell of Linux is Bash. The more modern and default shell of MacOS(since 2017) is zsh.

Common Linux commands include:

commanddescriptionexample
ls [dir]Lists files and folders in a given directory. Optional file path argument to specify directory to list, otherwise it will use the current working directory. You can use the “-l” flag to show a summary of the file/folder properties alongside the list.user@debian:~$ ls
Desktop Document Downloads Music Pictures Public Templates Videos
cd [dir]Changes the current working directory to the specified path.user@debian:~$cd Desktop
user@debian~/Desktop$

Cpu stress script

shell 
#!/bin/bash
#Get the number of CPU cores
CORES=$(nproc)

echo "Starting load on $CORES cores"
echo "Press Ctrl + C to stop the test"

# trap the exit signal to kill the background process only when you hit ctrl+c
trap 'kill 0' SIGINT

for i in $(seq 1 $CORES); do
  sha1sum /dev/zero > /dev/null &
done

# Keep the script running
wait
